title: Gateway: enforce hosted data residency at request admission (region pinning)
author: Amara Diallo
description: Implements API gateway request-admission enforcement for hosted data residency region pinning. This adds a middleware that evaluates the effective residency policy (pinned_region/allowed_regions + exception override) for each request before routing/model execution, and returns a standardized error payload when a request would execute in a non-approved region. The middleware also attaches residency decision context tags to the request context for downstream logging/metrics/tracing. Motivation: we need deterministic enforcement at the earliest possible point in the request path to prevent cross-region execution and any downstream side effects (e.g., traces/logs) when region pinning is enabled. This PR focuses on the gateway enforcement + error contract wiring; smart routing changes are handled separately (ENG-2843) but this PR will block requests that attempt to reach the wrong region (e.g., customer using us-east base URL while pinned to eu-west). Behavior summary: (1) If no residency policy is configured, middleware is a no-op (metrics still record "policy_absent"). (2) If pinned_region is configured, request_region must match pinned_region; cross-region fallback is not permitted here (router may have its own override later, but admission prevents wrong-region execution for standard hosted). (3) If allowed_regions is configured (no pinned), request_region must be within allowed_regions. (4) If an exception token/flag is present (from policy evaluator response) the request can proceed cross-region but is tagged as exception_granted=true and emits an audit event in later work (ENG-2844). Errors: returns HTTP 409 Conflict with error.code=RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH and a remediation message indicating which region is required, what the gateway observed, and a docs link. Also returns HTTP 503 Service Unavailable with error.code=RESIDENCY_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE when policy evaluator cannot be reached and the org is enterprise+residency_enforcement_enabled (fail closed); for non-enterprise / flag disabled, we fail open but tag decision=policy_unavailable_failopen. Includes minor refactor to standardize extraction of request_region from host header + explicit region header (x-redwood-region) (SDKs will set this), with precedence documented in code comments. References: ADR-043 (enforcement at gateway), error code taxonomy doc (data residency), and PR #18421 for policy schema/validation.
commits: gateway(residency): add residency enforcement middleware with policy evaluator client
gateway(errors): add RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH + POLICY_UNAVAILABLE mapping and docs link
gateway(context): attach residency decision tags to request context for tracing/logging
tests: unit tests for pinned/allowed policy evaluation + fail-open/fail-closed behavior
chore: config toggles + rollout flag plumbing for residency_enforcement_enabled
testing: Unit: services/gateway/test/residency_enforcement.test.ts (covers pinned_region match/mismatch; allowed_regions inclusion/exclusion; missing policy; explicit x-redwood-region header precedence; policy evaluator timeout handling). Manual: staging smoke test with an EU-pinned org calling us-east endpoint -> 409 RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH; same org calling eu-west endpoint -> 200; simulated policy evaluator outage -> enterprise org returns 503 POLICY_UNAVAILABLE; non-enterprise org fail-open (200) with decision tag policy_unavailable_failopen.
conversation: Brian Murphy (review): Can we confirm HTTP status for region mismatch? 403 vs 409 vs 400. Also please ensure error payload includes actionable fields for SDKs (required_region, request_region, policy_source).

Amara Diallo (author): Good call. Aligning with the residency error codes doc: 409 for conflict with org policy, and adding structured fields required_region/request_region/policy_scope (org/project). Pushed commit 2b9c6f7.

Marcus Lin (review): For enterprise accounts with enforcement enabled, we should fail closed if policy evaluator is unavailable. Please add explicit metrics + logs for fail-open decisions to help detect drift during beta.
Amara Diallo (author): Implemented fail-closed behind enforcement flag + enterprise tier check; added counter gateway_residency_policy_unavailable_total{mode=failopen|failclosed}. See commit 8af13d1.
Mina Haddad (review): How do we determine request_region? Host header vs x-redwood-region vs router-derived. We need deterministic precedence to avoid surprises.

Amara Diallo (author): Implemented precedence: explicit x-redwood-region header > parsed region from host > default region resolved from gateway deployment. Added tests + inline docs. Router will still validate later, but this should eliminate ambiguity.
Sean Gallagher (review): Any risk of noisy 5xx during rollout if policy evaluator has transient errors? Can we rate-limit logs and ensure SRE has a dashboard tag?

Amara Diallo (author): Added log sampling for POLICY_UNAVAILABLE and trace attribute residency.policy_eval_latency_ms + residency.decision. Follow-up ticket for dashboard wiring is ENG-2845, but the tags/counters are in this PR.
Ethan Park (review): Please confirm this runs before authentication? We need org id for policy lookup; ensure we don't call policy evaluator for unauthenticated requests.

Amara Diallo (author): Middleware runs after auth extraction (org resolved) but before routing/model selection. Unauthenticated requests short-circuit as before. Updated middleware chain comments accordingly.
Brian Murphy (review): Approving once payload shape matches API standards (snake_case) and docs link is stable.
Amara Diallo (author): Updated payload to match error contract conventions; docs link uses /docs/security/data-residency#region-mismatch. CI green.
Sean Gallagher (review): Approved (please ping when ENG-2845 dashboard lands).
release_notes: Hosted API: when data residency region pinning is enabled, requests sent to the wrong region are rejected at the gateway with a clear, machine-readable error (RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH) before any model execution.
notes: Follow-ups: ENG-2843 (routing no cross-region fallback when pinned), ENG-2844 (audit event emission), ENG-2845 (Grafana dashboard/alerts).
